guarantees.claim: c_inv is always driven by the output of aes_square_gf2p2 applied to c_buf[5].
r_sq is always driven by the output of aes_square_gf2p2 applied to r.

assumptions.claim: Input signals c_buf[5] and r are valid, non-x combinational values.
assumptions.risk: If either is x, c_inv or r_sq becomes x, corrupting downstream masked calculations.

assumptions.claim: The unmasked intermediate c_inv computed here must be re-masked (e.g., with (q1 ^ r_sq) and (q0 ^ q1) as per comments) in later logic before any security‑critical use.
assumptions.risk: Failure to re-mask would leave an unmasked intermediate, breaking the masked AES S‑box security property and possibly leaking secret data.

uncertain_points.claim: The re‑masking assignments described in comments (c_inv ^ (q1 ^ r_sq), c2_inv ^ (q0 ^ q1)) are not implemented in this chunk; they must exist in subsequent logic to preserve masking. If missing, unmasked intermediate c_inv could be used directly.
uncertain_points.cond: when c_inv is consumed downstream without re‑masking
uncertain_points.risk: Unmasked intermediate appears on a combinational path, potentially observable via side‑channel or logical propagation, compromising AES masking.
